counterevidence_considered.description: The only datum that could hint at a hidden repeated animal is that rows M10 and M20 share the same forewing length (17.4 mm). This does not demonstrate a repeated unit: the two rows carry distinct moth_id marks and different recorded sexes (female vs male), so they cannot be the same animal.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: M10 female 17.4 mm vs M20 male 17.4 mm

evidence.description: The data description defines the independent unit column as moth_id and states each animal was tested exactly once, so one row equals one independent unit.
evidence.observed_value: one row = one moth tested once; unit column moth_id

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one wild-caught hawkmoth tested a single time in the Y-tube choice arena
Independent unit column: moth_id
One trial is: one row

Every hawkmoth in this study was captured, given a unique mark, measured once,
released once into the Y-tube choice arena, scored, and then let go. No animal
entered the arena a second time, so the file is simply a list of animals, each
with the single choice it made.

evidence.description: Direct inspection of all 20 data rows shows moth_id values M01 through M20 are all distinct; no independent unit appears in more than one row.
The workflow explicitly validates uniqueness of the unit column and raises an error if any moth mark repeats, so a repeated-unit table could not even reach the binomial test.

The selected result reproduces from the data under the one-row-per-unit reading: 16 of 20 rows have chosen_spectrum amber, and the exact two-sided binomial p-value for 16/20 vs 0.5 is 12392/1048576 = 0.011818, matching the report; n = 20 in the test equals the number of distinct moth identifiers reported in the cohort table.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Two-sided exact binomial test of no spectral preference: 16 of 20 hawkmoths chose the amber arm (proportion 0.800 against a null of 0.500), p = 0.011818, so the preference for amber is statistically significant at alpha = 0.05.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by (a) scanning every moth_id in data/input.csv for duplicates (none; 20 distinct values in 20 rows), (b) looking for identical covariate profiles that could indicate the same animal re-entered under a different mark (the only shared forewing length, 17.4 mm in M10 and M20, belongs to rows with different sexes, ruling out a single animal), (c) checking whether the workflow could silently aggregate multiple rows per unit into the test (it cannot: read_trials raises ValueError on any repeated mark, and binomtest receives n_total = 20 row count equal to the 20 distinct marks), and (d) recomputing the selected result (16/20 amber, exact two-sided p = 0.011818) to confirm it matches the single-entry-per-unit data. No path to the issue class survived.
